There's a Hadith that says, "No one will be wronged and then take revenge except that it will be recorded against him on the Day of Judgment." So, that suggests that revenge isn't the right approach. Another point is the importance of forgiveness in Islam. The Prophet (peace be upon him) forgave those who wronged him, and we're encouraged to follow his example. Forgiving someone who has wronged you is seen as a noble act and can lead to positive outcomes. I also recall that Islam emphasizes the sanctity of relationships, especially family ties. Hurting a family member by damaging their property could strain the relationship, which is something to avoid. Maintaining good relations with family is important in Islam. So, putting it all together, Jill's action of taking revenge by damaging her cousin's car doesn't seem right according to Islamic teachings.
